topic: Fire of Rome (AD 64): flames break out among shops of flammable goods beside the Circus and, driven by wind through narrow twisting lanes, outrun every effort to stop them as fleeing crowds are trapped

research_sources.institution: LacusCurtius, University of Chicago (Tacitus, Annals 15.38-44, Loeb translation)
focus: swept the full length of the Circus

research_cautions: Do not assert Nero started the fire; Tacitus says it is uncertain whether it was chance or the emperor's malice.
No reliable death toll exists; do not invent one.
Nero was at Antium when it began; the 'fiddling' story is later legend.
